name: runtime_session
description_lines: Start, inspect, or stop a daemon-managed Godot runtime session.

`start` first runs scene-execution gates: C# projects run the same kind of explicit root .csproj Debug build Godot performs before Play, the scene runs structural validate_scene preflight without a headless runtime pass, and Fennara checks GDScript autoloads plus scene-attached GDScripts with targeted diagnostics.

Unlike the isolated compile-only build used by script_diagnostics scan_project:true, this runtime build updates .godot/mono/temp/bin/Debug so the launched scene uses the latest C# code. An already-open Godot editor may detect that assembly change and attempt its normal hot reload; Fennara does not close the editor.

For C# projects, start waits for any plugin-owned background C# preparation before running its authoritative runtime build. The wait occurs on a tool worker and does not block the Godot editor main thread.
If those gates fail, the scene is not opened.
Fennara exposes one machine-wide Runtime Slot, so at most one daemon-managed runtime session may be starting or running across all connected projects.

`status` without a remembered owner session is the cheap availability check. A free slot returns `{"ok":true,"status":"idle","availability":"free","slot_acquired":false}`. A slot claimed by another Project Root returns a successful anonymous result with `status:"busy"`, `availability:"busy"`, `slot_acquired:false`, and `retry_after_ms`; busy is a retryable domain result, not a tool error.

A busy result never reveals the owner, session id, process id, scene, artifacts, queue position, or expected duration. Wait at least retry_after_ms plus a small random jitter before polling again. Runtime Slot polling is best effort and has no FIFO guarantee.

`start` checks availability before expensive C# and scene/script preflight. A free check is advisory: after preflight, the daemon performs the final atomic claim, so a race loser can still receive anonymous busy without launching a process.
A successful start returns `status:"started"`, `availability:"busy"`, and `slot_acquired:true`. Keep its session_id for owner status, runtime_script, and stop calls.

The selected editor's canonical Project Root owns the Runtime Slot. Only that owner can inspect detailed status, renew the lease, run runtime_script, or stop the session. Another project receives anonymous busy without a session id, or `runtime_session_not_owned_or_found` when it names a session id.

Every start has an enforced absolute lease. max_run_seconds defaults to 900, must be a positive integer, and may not exceed 86400; for an expected one-hour regression, request 4500 seconds to leave a safety margin.

While a session should keep running, the owner should call status about every 30 seconds with jitter. Owner status renews a 120-second inactivity deadline. A bounded owner runtime operation suspends inactivity expiry while active and renews the deadline only after returning a terminal script result; timeout, setup error, or cancellation does not renew it. The absolute deadline never pauses.

Owner status reports absolute_deadline_ms, absolute_remaining_seconds, inactivity_deadline_ms, inactivity_remaining_seconds, and heartbeat_interval_ms. The inactivity fields are null while a bounded owner operation has suspended that deadline.

Natural exit, explicit stop, startup failure, inactivity expiry, or absolute expiry stops/reaps the process and releases the Runtime Slot. An owner receipt for either lease deadline includes code `runtime_lease_expired` and an exact end_reason. Stop promptly when runtime work is complete.
If gates pass, Fennara launches one scene from the selected/bound Godot project in a separate windowed Godot process with the runtime helper enabled.

Runtime sessions enable Godot's local debugger with error breaks ignored or auto-continued so debugger-aware addons can send debugger messages without requiring an attached editor session; normal errors and warnings are still captured in runtime_session.log.
The returned session_id can be reused for multiple runtime_script probes against the same running scene.
`start` saves one startup viewport capture under the session captures/ folder and, when the caller/model supports image input, returns that capture as image context in addition to the text receipt.
End the session with runtime_session.stop or with a final runtime_script that calls ctx.close_scene().
`status` and `stop` are operational receipts; a stopped process or non-zero exit code after an intentional stop is not by itself proof of a scene failure.
The returned runtime_session.log path is the full source of truth for scene startup output, runtime errors, runtime_script ctx.log output, capture events, and completion markers.

`start` requires both FENNARA_RUNTIME_SESSION_READY and the FENNARA_RUNTIME_ORIENTATION_NOTE startup orientation tail marker before its 20-second startup deadline. If either marker is missing at the deadline, the daemon kills and reaps the process before returning `status:"startup_timeout"`; it does not leave a runtime session running for a later status call.
Runtime receipts include a capped excerpt of new runtime log lines when available.

Fennara tracks a per-session log cursor: runtime_session, runtime_script, status, and stop results show log lines after the last remembered line, report omitted/truncated counts when capped, then advance the cursor to the current end of the log.
Read the full raw log when older history or omitted text matters.
Runtime sessions remain live between tool calls; after any planning delay, call owner status to renew the inactivity deadline and re-establish current state before acting.
Artifacts and raw stdout/stderr logs are saved under the current tool log directory.

action.description: The runtime session operation. `status` is safe anytime: without an owned session it reports anonymous machine-wide availability, while an owner receives detailed state and renews inactivity. `start` first short-circuits on busy, runs preflight when free, and then atomically claims the Runtime Slot; it can still return successful anonymous busy if another caller wins that race. After spawn, `start` succeeds only if both runtime-ready and orientation markers arrive before the 20-second startup deadline; otherwise the daemon kills and reaps the process before returning `startup_timeout`. `stop` closes the owning project's running session and releases the slot. Treat owner status/stop results as process receipts; for scene behavior and failure evidence, use the returned runtime log update and read the full runtime_session.log when older history or omitted text matters.

scene_path.description: Required for action `start`. The exact `res://` path to a `.tscn` scene to play.

user_args.description: Optional for action `start`. Project-specific arguments passed unchanged after Godot's `--` separator. The running project receives them through `OS.get_cmdline_user_args()`.

max_run_seconds.description: Optional for action `start`. Enforced absolute lease in whole seconds; defaults to 900 (15 minutes), must be positive, and may not exceed 86400 (24 hours). Choose a value that covers the expected run plus cleanup margin; an expected one-hour regression may use 4500. The absolute deadline never pauses, so still stop promptly when done.

session_id.description: Optional for action `status` or `stop`. The managed runtime session id returned to this Project Root by `runtime_session.start`. With no remembered owner session, omitted status queries anonymous Runtime Slot availability instead of fabricating local idle. Pass the id for recovery or explicit owner control. A different Project Root cannot inspect or control the session and receives `runtime_session_not_owned_or_found` rather than evidence that the id exists.
